penalties_applied.name: requires_synchronous_human
penalties_applied.reason: Meaningful career coaching or curriculum delivery typically requires live sessions, cohort calls, or at minimum synchronous check-ins to be credible and retain customers — hard to fully automate.

penalties_applied.name: high_touch_support
penalties_applied.reason: Career-transition customers have high anxiety and expect ongoing responsiveness; async-only support risks churn and refund demands.

rationale: The buyer is a mid-to-senior software engineer — an individual consumer, not a business with a budget line — and while career-transition services can command high prices, willingness to pay in this cohort is unproven and highly variable (many expect free content from YouTube/blogs). Operational autonomy is the fatal flaw: credible career coaching requires synchronous human involvement (calls, feedback, cohort energy), and an async Claude curriculum alone is unlikely to convert or retain paying customers at $500+. The signal source is a single reflective HN post, not a buying signal.
solution_plan: Not recommended to build. A solo non-technical operator cannot credibly deliver career coaching at a price point that justifies the effort without significant synchronous human involvement (calls, cohort management, personalized feedback). The async-only version (a PDF guide or Claude chatbot) competes with free resources and would not retain paying customers. If revisiting, validate first: post a $49 async 'AI career audit' offer in a developer Slack and see if anyone buys without a sales call.
notes: Fails operational_autonomy gate (score 3, minimum 7). Fails buyer_clarity gate (score 5, minimum 6). Total 3.1 is below min_total_to_validate (5.5). Drop.
